faq.q: What could make an appliance's case live?
faq.a: Inside a metal kettle, toaster or washing machine, a live wire can work loose, or worn insulation can let it touch the metal case. Then the case itself carries mains voltage.
asks: How does a metal case become dangerous?

faq.q: Why is touching a live case dangerous?
faq.a: Your body would become a path from the live case to the ground, and mains voltage can push a dangerous current through you, including through your heart.
asks: What happens if you touch a live appliance?

faq.q: What does the earth wire do?
faq.a: The green and yellow earth wire joins the metal case to the ground through the house wiring. Its very low resistance gives the current a much easier path than through a person.
asks: What colour is the earth wire?

faq.q: Why does the fuse blow when the case touches live?
faq.a: The earth wire has almost no resistance, so a huge current rushes from live to earth. That melts the fuse or trips the breaker, cutting off the power.
asks: How does earthing cut the power?

faq.q: Why do some appliances have no earth wire?
faq.a: Double-insulated appliances, like many hairdryers and phone chargers, have plastic cases and an extra layer of insulation, so no live part can touch anything you hold. They carry a symbol of a square inside a square.
asks: What does the square in a square symbol mean?

facts: In UK plugs the earth wire is green and yellow, the live is brown and the neutral is blue.
Double-insulated appliances are marked with a square inside a square and need no earth wire.

quiz.say: When a live wire touches an earthed metal case, what happens next?
quiz.show: When a live wire touches an earthed metal case, what happens next?

options.show: A big current flows to earth and the fuse blows
options.say: A big current flows to earth and the fuse blows

options.show: Nothing, because the case is metal
options.say: Nothing, because the case is metal

quiz.why: The earth wire's low resistance lets a large current flow, which melts the fuse or trips the breaker and cuts the power.

wrong.1: A fault never makes an appliance work better.
wrong.2: Metal conducts, which is exactly why a live metal case is dangerous without earthing.
